title: rx.match: state vars in case conditions (component branches) emit unbound useContext → ReferenceError: Can't find variable: <substate>
body:
## Description

When `rx.match(...)` returns **components** in its cases and a **state var is used in a case _condition_** (e.g. `(MyState.x > 0, some_component)`), the compiled page references the substate's React context variable but never emits the matching `useContext(...)` binding. At render the browser throws:

```
ReferenceError: Can't find variable: reflex___state____state__<app>___states___<module>____<state>
```

This happens whenever a state var appears only in the match **conditions** (not in the subject) with component return values — most commonly via the idiomatic "match on a literal subject" pattern:

```python
rx.match(True, (State.x > 0, comp_a), (State.y > 0, comp_b), default_comp)
```

## Minimal reproduction

`rxconfig.py`:

```python
import reflex as rx

config = rx.Config(app_name="rx_match_repro")
```

`rx_match_repro/rx_match_repro.py`:

```python
import reflex as rx


class MatchState(rx.State):
    a: int = 0
    b: int = 0


def index() -> rx.Component:
    return rx.match(
        True,
        (MatchState.a > 0, rx.text("a positive")),
        (MatchState.b > 0, rx.text("b positive")),
        rx.text("neither"),
    )


app = rx.App()
app.add_page(index)
```

`reflex run` and open `/` → blank page, and the browser console shows:

```
ReferenceError: Can't find variable: reflex___state____state__rx_match_repro___rx_match_repro____match_state
```

## Compiled output (the bug)

`.web/app/routes/_index.jsx` (reflex `0.9.5.post2`):

```jsx
export default function Component() {
  return (
    jsx(Fragment,{},jsx(Fragment,{},(() => {
  switch (JSON.stringify(true)) {
    case JSON.stringify((reflex___state____state__rx_match_repro___rx_match_repro____match_state.a_rx_state_ > 0)):
      return jsx(RadixThemesText,{as:"p"},"a positive");
    case JSON.stringify((reflex___state____state__rx_match_repro___rx_match_repro____match_state.b_rx_state_ > 0)):
      return jsx(RadixThemesText,{as:"p"},"b positive");
    default:
      return jsx(RadixThemesText,{as:"p"},"neither");
  }
})()), ... )
  )
}
```

`Component()` references `reflex___state____state__...____match_state` in the `switch` cases but contains **no** `const ... = useContext(StateContexts....)` binding (`grep -c useContext _index.jsx` → `0`). Hence the `ReferenceError` on first render.

For contrast, `rx.cond`/`rx.foreach` are extracted into memoized child components that each emit their own `useContext` binding, so they work.

## Root cause

`reflex_components_core/core/match.py`, `Match._create_match_cond_var_or_component`:

The **Var-return** branch merges the case-condition var-data correctly:

```python
return Var(
    _js_expr=format.format_match(...),
    _var_type=default._var_type,
    _var_data=VarData.merge(
        match_cond_var._get_all_var_data(),
        *[el._get_all_var_data() for case in match_cases for el in case[0]],  # <-- conditions
        *[case[1]._get_all_var_data() for case in match_cases],
        default._get_all_var_data(),
    ),
)
```

But the **BaseComponent-return** branch does **not** propagate the subject/condition var-data to the rendered Match component — it only forwards the branch components as `children`:

```python
if isinstance(match_cases[0][1], BaseComponent):
    if default is None:
        default = Fragment.create()
    return Fragment.create(
        cls._create(
            cond=match_cond_var,
            match_cases=match_cases,
            default=default,
            children=[case[1] for case in match_cases] + [default],  # only branch components
        )
    )
```

So for component branches, the var-data (hooks/imports — including the `useContext` for any substate referenced in the `case[0]` conditions, and the subject) is never hoisted into the page `Component`. With a literal subject the subject contributes no var-data either, so nothing is emitted at all and the condition references are left unbound.

Likely related to the earlier #2393 ("Need to recursively enumerate VarData for all rx.match components"), which addressed return values; the **condition** var-data in the component branch still appears to be dropped.

## Expected behavior

The compiler should emit the `useContext` binding for any substate referenced in `rx.match` case conditions when the branches are components (e.g. include the condition vars in the Match component's `_get_vars()` / var-data), so the page renders instead of throwing a `ReferenceError`. Alternatively, reject a constant subject combined with state-var case conditions at compile time.

## Workaround

Replace the `rx.match` with chained `rx.cond` (which compiles to child components that each bind `useContext`):

```python
rx.cond(
    MatchState.a > 0,
    rx.text("a positive"),
    rx.cond(MatchState.b > 0, rx.text("b positive"), rx.text("neither")),
)
```

## Environment

- Reflex `0.9.5.post2` (`reflex-components-core` — `core/match.py`)
- Python 3.13
- Reproduces in a local `reflex run` and on Reflex Cloud deploys.

title: Carry client state hooks on ClientStateVar setters
body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> **This is a stopgap fix.** It is meant to unblock users until the real `ClientStateVar` refactor lands. The refactor will handle this case much more cleanly and **without creating extra React states** in components that only set the value. Treat this change as temporary: the refactor should replace it rather than build on it.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

### Description

Users reported frontend errors when sibling components share a global `rx._x.client_state` var (`global_ref=True`): one sibling renders `.value` and another sets it from a user interaction.

**Root cause:** `ClientStateVar.set` / `set_value()` returned a Var that referenced `refs['_client_state_set<name>']` but didn't carry the `useState`/`useId`/`refs` hooks that define it. Auto-memoization compiles the setter-only sibling into its own memo body, so the setter only worked if a component rendering `.value` had already mounted and defined the function. When no reader was mounted (for example, the reader sits behind an `rx.cond`), the setter threw:

```
TypeError: refs._client_state_set<name> is not a function
```

**Fix:**
- For global vars (`global_ref=True`), the setter Var now carries the `ClientStateVar`'s `VarData`. Every component that sets the value registers its own `useState` instance in the shared `refs` setter dict, and the global setter fans out to all of them.
- `create()` now keeps the default's full `VarData`, so a backend-derived default (`default=State.field`) brings its state `useContext` hook along.
- Local vars (`global_ref=False`) are unchanged. A setter-only sibling still fails loudly with `setX is not defined`, instead of silently updating a private copy of the state that no reader sees.

**Trade-offs of this stopgap (all addressed by the upcoming refactor):**
- Components that only set the value now hold an extra `useState` and re-render when the value changes.
- The setter's `useCallback` now lists the client-state hook values as dependencies, so it is recreated on every value change.
- With a backend-derived default (`default=State.field`), a setter-only component now also subscribes to that whole backend state through `useContext`. It re-renders, and recreates its `onClick`, on every delta to any field of that state, even though `useState` only reads the default on mount.
- Setter-only components also add an entry to `refs['_client_state_dict_set<name>']` that is never removed on unmount, as readers already did before this PR. Every set call still invokes the setters of unmounted components.

### Follow-ups for the `ClientStateVar` refactor

These are out of scope for this stopgap:
- Don't give setter-only components their own React state.
- Don't subscribe setter-only components to the default's backend state after mount.
- Remove per-instance entries from the setter and value dicts on unmount (e.g. `useEffect` cleanup).
- Allow backend `push()` / `retrieve()` to work when no component using the var is mounted. Today `run_script` can't carry hooks, so both require a mounted component. This is unchanged by this PR.
- Local (`global_ref=False`) vars still can't be shared between components that auto-memoize separately. This is inherent to local state and unchanged by this PR.

### Tests

- `tests/units/experimental/test_client_state.py` (new):
  - Global setters carry the client state hooks, for both `.set` and `.set_value(...)`.
  - Local setters don't carry them.
  - A backend-derived default's hooks reach `.value`, `.set` and `.set_value(...)`.
- `tests/units/compiler/test_memoize_plugin.py`: the memo for a setter-only sibling contains `useState` and defines the `refs` setter.
- `tests/integration/tests_playwright/test_client_state.py` (new): browser tests for three cases:
  - siblings that are both mounted
  - a setter clicked before its reader mounts behind an `rx.cond`
  - a backend-derived default with a sibling setter

The unit tests, the cond-reader browser test and the backend-default browser test fail without their fixes and pass with them. The both-mounted browser test also passed before the fix and is kept as a guard. The full unit suite passes, and ruff and pyright are clean.

title: Rejected token with `--no-interactive` still opens the browser login prompt
body:
**Package:** `reflex-hosting-cli` (reproduced on `main` at `ea035ea47` and on #7207 at `988718e78`)

When `REFLEX_ACCESS_TOKEN` holds an invalid token, a command run with `--no-interactive` starts the browser login flow and waits for Enter:

```
$ REFLEX_ACCESS_TOKEN=bogus-token reflex cloud apps list --no-interactive
... https://build.reflex.dev/cli/login?request_id=... to authenticate.
please hit 'Enter' or 'Return' after login on website complete:
```

On `main` it then prints `Unable to list deployments`; on #7207 it prints `Aborted!`. Both exit 1, but only after the prompt, which hangs CI when stdin is a TTY or stays open.

`whoami` already does the right thing with the same token:

```
$ REFLEX_ACCESS_TOKEN=bogus-token reflex cloud whoami
The access token from the REFLEX_ACCESS_TOKEN environment variable was rejected: access denied (...)
[exit=1]
```

Without any token, `--no-interactive` also fails fast (`Token is required for non-interactive mode.`).

**Expected:** with `--no-interactive`, a rejected token fails immediately, with the same message `whoami` gives. The interactive login is never offered.

title: Render state contexts without a component per substate on the server
body: ### All Submissions: - [x] Have you followed the guidelines stated in [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/reflex-dev/reflex/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) file? - [x] Have you checked to ensure there aren't any other open [Pull Requests](https://github.com/reflex-dev/reflex/pulls) for the desired changed? ### Type of change - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) ### Changes To Core Features: - [x] Have you added an explanation of what your changes do and why you'd like us to include them? - [x] Have you written new tests for your core changes, as applicable? - [x] Have you successfully ran tests with your changes locally? ## What and why #6181 gave every substate its own `SubstateProvider` so a delta re-renders only the contexts it changes. On the server that component has no job (the page renders once and no delta is ever applied), but it adds a second render level per substate. React's server renderer recurses once per level, so the depth of every page render doubled. In an app with ~150 substates this intermittently failed **every route** in the dev server with a 500 (`Unexpected Server Error` / `SyntaxError: Invalid regular expression: /[^a-z-]/: Stack overflow`) that cleared on its own after 40–60 s. Measured on that app: - Before V8 has optimised React's render functions (after a restart, and again after a major GC), the render reaches the first Emotion `css` element 1,254 frames deep with about 7 KB of the default ~984 KB stack left. - React Fizz recovers from overflows whose message is exactly `Maximum call stack size exceeded`: it re-renders that subtree from a fresh stack. An overflow that surfaces as anything else is not recovered, and the request fails. The regex `SyntaxError` above is one example; a `TypeError` reading `$$typeof` on a `useContext` is another. - Running the same app with the stack only 1–2.5% smaller (`--stack-size=971` and `960`) reproduced the 500s reliably, including the fail-then-recover pattern. ## Change `context_template` now emits the substates once as a `SUBSTATES` table, plus two providers chosen at module load: - **`ClientStateProvider`** (browser): unchanged behaviour. `DispatchProvider` and one `SubstateProvider` per substate, memoized on `children`, built with a loop instead of a generated nested expression. - **`ServerStateProvider`** (`typeof document === "undefined"`, the same test `useIsomorphicLayoutEffect` uses): bare context providers carrying `initialState`, one level per substate. No reducers or dispatch registry, because nothing dispatches on the server. Hydration is unaffected: wrapper components produce no DOM and do not fork the tree. In the app above there were no hydration warnings on any page, with the same console output as before the change. Same app, with the fix: | | Before | After | |---|---|---| | Depth of first `css` element | 1,254 frames | 646 frames | | Stack free on a cold render | ~0.7% | ~45% | | `--stack-size` 950–990 KB and 960/971 | 500s at 960 and 971 | all clean | | `--stack-size` down to 500 KB | not tested | all clean | ## Tests - `test_context_template_server_state_provider_is_flat` (new) and the updated `test_context_template_one_provider_per_substate` fail on `main` and pass here. - `test_context_js_template.py` located `EventLoopProvider` by the old `export function StateProvider` text; it now anchors on the next declaration. - `tests/units/compiler`: 308 passed. The full unit suite has the same failures with and without this change (227 `reflex_cli` tests that fail in my environment on clean `main` too). - `tests/integration/tests_playwright/test_router_query.py`: 8 passed in dev and prod, including #6181's case where one delta updates two sibling substates. - pre-commit hooks pass on the changed files. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01CQ4shGzkLwvScpUv6vxqHm --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_01CQ4shGzkLwvScpUv6vxqHm)_

title: Refresh framework dependencies ahead of 0.10.0
body: Refresh the framework's frontend pins and locked backend dependencies ahead of Reflex 0.10.0. Generated apps use React 19.3, Vite 8.3.2, Bun 1.4.2, and updated Socket.IO, Shiki, Moment, Radix, upload, and error-boundary packages. Locked backend updates include Starlette 1.7, Granian 2.8.3, Pydantic 2.13.5, python-socketio 5.17, and wrapt 2.5. Refresh the uv and docs Bun lockfiles and add news fragments for all six affected packages. Preserve all existing dependency lower bounds, including workspace sibling floors; the framework does not require newer library APIs. Regenerating component stubs leaves `pyi_hashes.json` unchanged. ### Compatibility - Preserve the existing Redis, Plotly, Tailwind, and externally owned frontend holds, and retain the seven-day backend release delay. - Update react-dropzone to 17.0.0; hold 18+ because they change MIME fallback handling and over-limit upload batch acceptance. - Widen the wrapt upper bound to `<2.6` to allow 2.4 and 2.5. - Lock SQLModel to 0.0.44 and cap it below 0.0.45. The newer default UTC storage rejects existing naive datetime values; the existing migration test reproduced the break. - Remove the obsolete react-moment hold and update version-sensitive test fixtures. ### Validation - Full unit suite on Python 3.14.6 with Node 22.22.3: **11,252 passed, 159 skipped; 78.99% coverage**. - Existing upload and Moment browser integration tests: **18 passed**. - Temporary production app with a fresh Bun 1.4.2 installation: build, Shiki rendering, Radix slider/progress, upload, Moment, and Socket.IO state event roundtrip passed. - Dependency checker tests after restoring the original floors: **91 passed**; verified all original lower bounds and resolved package versions are preserved. - Minimum-dependency checks for `reflex` and `reflex-base` on Python 3.10 passed. - Ruff lint, formatting, and `pyright reflex tests` passed. - Adversarial diff review completed with no remaining findings. The all-files pre-commit run stops at six macOS typing errors in unchanged Linux benchmark code (`sched_setaffinity`, `sched_getaffinity`, and `psutil.Process.cpu_affinity`). The required `pyright reflex tests` check passes. Staged-file pre-commit hooks passed, including codespell, stub generation, pyright, and ty.

description.body: ### All Submissions: - [x] Have you followed the guidelines stated in [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/reflex-dev/reflex/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) file? - [x] Have you checked to ensure there aren't any other open [Pull Requests](https://github.com/reflex-dev/reflex/pulls) for the desired changed? ### Type of change - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) ### Changes To Core Features: - [x] Have you added an explanation of what your changes do and why you'd like us to include them? - [x] Have you written new tests for your core changes, as applicable? - [x] Have you successfully ran tests with your changes locally? ## What goes wrong When `rx.download` gets a state Var as `data`, it builds the URL as `"data:," + JSON.stringify(var)` and does not percent-encode it. In a `data:` URL, `#` starts the fragment, so everything after the first `#` in the JSON is dropped, and `%XX` sequences are decoded. The documented table example (`rx.download(data=TableDownloadState.users, filename="data.json")`, in `docs/library/tables-and-data-grids/table.md`) therefore downloads a truncated, invalid JSON file whenever a row contains a `#`, such as an address like `12 Main St #4` or a hex color. Node's `fetch` follows the same data-URL rules as the browser: ``` data = [{"address": "12 Main St #4", "note": "100%25 sure"}] before: [{"address":"12 Main St after: [{"address":"12 Main St #4","note":"100%25 sure"}] ``` ## Fix Wrap the stringified value in `encodeURIComponent(...)`. Data that is already a `data:` URI is still passed through unchanged. The `str` and `bytes` paths already base64-encode their data, so they don't change. ## Tests - `tests/units/test_event.py::test_download_var_data_is_percent_encoded` pins the generated expression. - `tests/units/test_event.py::test_download_var_data_url_keeps_hash_and_percent` evaluates the generated URL in Node, which the test skips if Node isn't installed, as `tests/units/reflex_base/test_client_event_queue.py` does. It reads the URL back with `fetch` and asserts the bytes are exactly the original JSON. - Both fail on `main` (`fe2a78f4`). The Node test fails with `JSONDecodeError: Unterminated string` because the download was cut off at `#`. Both pass with the fix. Checks, all run locally: - `uv run pytest tests/units`: 9845 passed. - `pre-commit run --from-ref HEAD~1 --to-ref HEAD`: ruff-format, ruff-check, codespell, update-pyi-files, pyright and ty all pass. - A news fragment is added under `packages/reflex-base/news/`. AI disclosure: an AI agent (Claude) found this bug and wrote the patch and tests, operating the `breken-ai` account. I reviewed the diff adversarially before opening this PR. I'll respond to review feedback, including Greptile/Copilot.
description.title: fix: percent-encode Var data in rx.download so # and % don't corrupt the file

description.body:
Skip shared-state fan-out when no affected client tokens were collected. Apps that define `rx.SharedState` avoid the unnecessary registered-App lookup when there are no other clients to update.

Add benchmarks for private counters, linked counters, multi-client fan-out, `app.modify_state`, and link/unlink cycles. Benchmark state registration and shared-state flags are isolated so collecting or running these scenarios does not change ordinary event-processing benchmarks. Fan-out waits have a timeout, and scenario teardown drains pending updates before closing the state manager.

Regression tests cover the empty fan-out guard, benchmark isolation, and stalled-update cleanup. The internal-state construction in the guard test also type-checks against current `main`.

Validation: full unit suite with coverage, all pre-commit hooks, the CodSpeed benchmark suite, and targeted tests on current `main`. A real app was also exercised across three independent browser clients for linking, room isolation, unlink/relink, background and API updates, computed values, and multiple shared-state classes.
description.title: Skip shared-state fan-out when no clients need updates

description.body: ### All Submissions: - [x] Have you followed the guidelines stated in [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/reflex-dev/reflex/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) file? - [x] Have you checked to ensure there aren't any other open [Pull Requests](https://github.com/reflex-dev/reflex/pulls) for the desired changed? ### Type of change - [x] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [x] This change requires a documentation update Part 1 of 4 of #7302. Stack: **1 field descriptors** → 2 state locks → 3 core state in reflex-base → 4 `dispatch_value`. ### Description Replaces `BaseState._get_attribute` and the `__setattr__` routing with real descriptors: - `Field` is a data descriptor bound to the class that declares it. It stores the value in the owning state's `__dict__`, fills in defaults lazily, type-checks, wraps mutable values in `MutableProxy` and marks itself dirty. `ComputedVar` and `EventHandler` also resolve through descriptors. - Inheritance works like plain Python: an inherited var resolves to the ancestor state that owns it. Redeclaring a var in a substate makes an independent var, and the var-vs-var shadowing errors are gone. The reserved-name check stays. - A write invalidates only the computed vars that depend on the changed var, instead of recomputing all of them. - Bookkeeping (`parent_state`, `substates`, `dirty_vars` and the like) moves into `__slots__`, out of the pickled dict. Pickles from the previous release still load. Pickles written now also carry compatibility keys, so workers still on the previous release can load them during a rolling deploy. - Delta building moves to `reflex/istate/delta.py`, and `get_delta` only looks at fields. - The undeclared-attribute typo guard runs only outside prod mode. In prod mode, state var reads go from about 1050 ns to about 250 ns, and writes from about 9.8 µs to about 660 ns (`tests/benchmarks/test_state_access.py`). Breaking: internals like `_get_attribute`, `get_skip_vars`, `backend_vars`, `inherited_vars`, `_dirty_computed_vars`, `is_backend_base_variable` and `RESERVED_BACKEND_VAR_NAMES` are removed. The news fragments list the rest. ### Changes To Core Features: - [x] Have you added an explanation of what your changes do and why you'd like us to include them? - [x] Have you written new tests for your core changes, as applicable? - [x] Have you successfully ran tests with your changes locally? 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_0145YmAVjKSJhdUFDcBP4FB9 --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_0145YmAVjKSJhdUFDcBP4FB9)_

description.body: ## Summary Supersedes #6743. That PR is stacked on #6735, which was closed without merging, and it conflicts with main. Most of it is already covered on main: | Part of #6743 | Status on main | |---|---| | Dirty-propagation frontier | Covered by #7312: `Field.__set__` calls `_mark_dirty((name,))`, so a write walks only the dependents of the var that changed. | | `_interval_computed_vars` | Covered by #7025 (`_interval_computed_var_names`). | | Return-type check on recompute only | **This PR.** | | Shallow type check in prod | **This PR.** | | Per-field `MutableProxy` cache | Left out. See below. | ### Changes 1. **A cached computed var checks its return type only when it recomputes** (sync and async). Before, every read ran `_check_deprecated_return_type` with `nested=1`, even on a cache hit, in every mode. 2. **In prod mode, state var assignments and computed var results check only the outer type** (`nested=0`). The check only logs an error. Dev mode keeps the element check. The mode is read from `REFLEX_ENV_MODE` on each call, with an exact comparison that matches the canonical enum parser. `environment.REFLEX_ENV_MODE.get()` costs about 2.4 µs, too much for every write. Scalar values never reach this check, because `_plain_types` short-circuits first. ### Measurements Micro-benchmarks, in-process, py3.14, median of 15: | | main | this PR | |---|---|---| | Read a cached computed var returning about 250 dicts (any mode) | 321 µs | 0.43 µs | | Assign a list of 500 dicts (prod) | 248 µs | 2.6 µs | | Assign a list of 500 dicts (dev) | 247 µs | 248 µs | | Assign an `int` (prod) | 2.5 µs | 2.6 µs | End to end, over a websocket: prod backend, one granian worker, server and client on separate pinned cores. There were 7 interleaved rounds of 2,000 serial events (600 for the reassign). Values are the median and [min–max] of the 7 rounds: | Handler | main p50 RTT | this PR p50 RTT | CPU per event | |---|---|---|---| | Reassign a 500-row list + dependent computed var | 2651 [2541–3099] µs | 2156 [2114–2179] µs | **−18%**, 7/7 rounds | | `count += 1`, list append, nested mutation, substate | — | — | no change expected. Moves of ±5–12% in both directions are run-to-run noise, because this diff does not touch those paths. | The win shows only for handlers that assign large containers or read cached computed vars. Typical scalar and in-place mutation events do not change. ### Not included: the proxy cache In the same A/B, caching the top-level `MutableProxy` per field saved about 1.1 µs per read. It gave −13% only in a handler that read `self.items` 50 times, and nothing on append or nested mutation. It also changes behavior: two reads return the same proxy, so overlapping `async with self.items` blocks now raise `RuntimeError: Mutable proxy is already in an async context`. It also needs an extra slot and an extra `pop` on every tracked write. Background tasks get no benefit, because `StateProxy` re-wraps on every read. ## Tests - New tests in `tests/units/reflex_base/vars/test_base.py` fail on main and pass here: - A sync or async cached computed var checks its return type once per recompute. - The element-type error is logged in dev and not in prod. - The outer-type error is logged in both modes. - `uv run pytest tests/units`: 11043 passed. - ruff, pyright and pre-commit are clean.

description.body:
Since #7136, a state that mixes in `abc.ABC` fails at class creation:

```python
class Mixin(ABC, rx.State, mixin=True):
    @abstractmethod
    def _value(self) -> int: ...
# StateValueError: State name `_abc_impl` is reserved by BaseState; use a different name instead.
```

`BaseStateMeta` is an `ABCMeta`, so `BaseState` has its own `_abc_impl`, and the reserved-name check then flags the `_abc_impl` it finds in `vars(ABC)` (and in any other `ABCMeta` mixin). `ABCMeta` writes `_abc_impl` onto every class it creates, so the copy an `ABC` mixin carries is bookkeeping, not a declaration. This change skips it only where it is inherited from a non-state base: declaring or `add_var`-ing `_abc_impl` on a state is still rejected. The tests cover `ABC` both as a plain mixin and under a state mixin, check that abstract methods are still enforced, and keep the reserved-name error for a state's own `_abc_impl`.
description.title: Allow ABC mixins on states despite ABCMeta's _abc_impl bookkeeping

## Summary
- Removes the duplicate `BaseContext` defined in `reflex_base.plugins.compiler` and points `PageContext` / `CompileContext` at the canonical `reflex_base.context.base.BaseContext`.
- Reworks `BaseContext` from a frozen dataclass into a plain class with `__slots__ = ()`, so frozen subclasses (`RegistrationContext`, `EventContext`, `TelemetryContext`) and non-frozen subclasses (`PageContext`, `CompileContext`) can both inherit from it. Each subclass keeps the `frozen` / `slots` / `eq` settings of its own `@dataclass` decorator; `PageContext` / `CompileContext` are now fully slotted, since the base no longer contributes a `__dict__`.
- Keys the class-level attached-token registry by `id(self)` instead of `self`, so instances with equal fields (including `eq=True` subclasses like `PageContext` / `CompileContext`) are entered and nested independently, whatever the subclass's `eq` setting.
- `ensure_context_attached()` now requires the instance to be the *active* context in the current `contextvars` context, not merely attached somewhere.
- Ports the async `__aenter__` / `__aexit__` helpers over from the removed compiler copy.
- **Breaking:** `PageContext.get()` and `CompileContext.get()` now raise `LookupError` instead of `RuntimeError` when no context is active, matching every other `BaseContext` subclass (news fragment `packages/reflex-base/news/6553.breaking.md`).
- Tests: updates `tests/units/compiler/test_plugins.py` for the new error types / `_context_var` name, and adds `tests/units/reflex_base/context/test_base.py` coverage for inactive-instance and cross-context `ensure_context_attached`, field-equal instances nesting (frozen and non-frozen), and the async context manager.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

### Changes To Core Features

- [x] Have you added an explanation of what your changes do and why you'd like us to include them?
- [x] Have you written new tests for your core changes, as applicable?
- [x] Have you successfully ran tests with your changes locally?

### Description

**Problem:** every top-level event is a fork of the event processor's root context, so its `parent_txid` was the root context's random txid. No future is ever registered under that txid, so event chaining was unaffected. But an event enqueued while a local span is current becomes an `INTERNAL` span, and `otel.event_span` recorded that meaningless txid as its `reflex.event.parent_txid`. Two ways this happens, both under the OpenTelemetry ASGI middleware's request span:
- the chunked upload endpoint (`_upload_chunk_file`);
- a custom API route calling `app.event_processor.enqueue`.

Websocket events escaped this only because they are `CONSUMER` spans. reflex-dev/reflex#7357 fixed `enqueue_stream_delta`; the general case remained.

**Solution:** fix it where the txid comes from rather than at call sites:
1. `EventProcessor.configure()` gives the root context an empty txid, since it belongs to no event.
2. `EventContext.fork()` sets `parent_txid=self.txid or None`, so forks of a context without a txid are top-level events.

`enqueue` already skips the parent-future lookup for a `None` parent. Top-level events still start their own root generation (supersession unchanged), and chained events still find their parent's future. `enqueue_stream_delta` already builds its stream context fresh (from reflex-dev/reflex#7357), so only its comment changed. That now matters for one more reason: a copy of the root would have no txid, and the events the stream's handler chains could not find the stream's future.

### Tests

- `test_top_level_event_under_local_span_names_no_parent_event`: enqueues a chaining event under a local `POST /api` span. The top-level span is `INTERNAL` under the request span with no `reflex.event.parent_txid`, the chained span still names the top-level event, and the future tree is unchanged. Fails before the fix: the attribute holds the root context's txid.
- `test_fork_without_txid_has_no_parent`: `fork()` of a context without a txid gives `parent_txid=None`, and a fork of that fork names it. Fails before the fix (`'' is not None`).
- `test_stream_delta_waits_for_chained_events`: the stream ends only once its handler's chained events are done.
  - It fails if the stream context loses its own txid.
  - `test_stream_delta_yields_chained_event_deltas` still passes in that case, because its chained event finishes before the stream closes.

Locally:
- `uv run pytest tests/units/reflex_base`: 561 passed.
- Full `tests/units`: 11030 passed, 81.24% coverage. This excludes `tests/units/reflex_bench/drivers/test_browser.py`, which fails the same way without this change because the container lacks the pinned Playwright browser build.
- ruff, pyright and the pre-commit hooks pass.

### Not changed

- `App.modify_state` forks the current context to rebind the token. An event enqueued inside `async with app.modify_state(...)` still names that fork's txid, which belongs to no event either. Changing that would alter chaining for handlers that call `app.modify_state`.
- Root contexts built directly (the `mock_root_event_context` fixture, the benchmark roots) keep a random txid, so their forks still name it. Harmless: nothing is registered under it.
- `EventContext.get().txid` outside any event is now `""` instead of a process-constant random id. Nothing in the repo reads it.

description.body:
### All Submissions:

- [x] Have you followed the guidelines stated in [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/reflex-dev/reflex/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) file?
- [x] Have you checked to ensure there aren't any other open [Pull Requests](https://github.com/reflex-dev/reflex/pulls) for the desired changed?

### Type of change

- [x] Performance improvement (non-breaking for apps; the frontend/backend boot protocol changes, which the existing version-subprotocol check already requires to match)

### Changes To Core Features:

- [x] Have you added an explanation of what your changes do and why you'd like us to include them?
- [x] Have you written new tests for your core changes, as applicable?
- [x] Have you successfully ran tests with your changes locally?

## What changes

First load of a Reflex app used to be: HTML, JS, websocket upgrade, wait for the socket.io connect ack, then three events (`hydrate`, `update_vars_internal`, `on_load_internal`), each its own state lock cycle, with `hydrate` serializing every var of every substate even though the bundle already carries the same defaults.

Now:

- **One boot event, inside the connect packet.** The frontend sends a single `hydrate_and_load` event as socket.io `auth`, so the backend starts loading state as soon as the namespace connects, one round trip earlier. The event resets and applies client storage and snapshots the state under one lock. For a page with `on_load` handlers it then chains `on_load_internal`, which locks only its leaf substate and still supersedes, so a navigation can cancel stale page-load work but never the snapshot. Enqueuing the boot event also cancels the previous page's unfinished `on_load` chain (as the connect's `on_load_internal` did before), without the boot event itself being cancellable.
- **Diff against the compiled defaults.** On the first hydrate of a page the frontend sends a digest of its compiled state names plus short per-state hashes of its compiled `initialState`; for every state whose compiled defaults match the backend's, only vars that differ are sent. Reconnects and storage resets still get the full state. States defined after the snapshot was taken (dynamic component states) invalidate the cached snapshot; unknown states and malformed hash lists are sent in full.
- **Fewer redis operations per load.** A state-tree save is now one server-side script that checks the lock and writes every touched substate atomically (one round trip instead of a lock GET, a PTTL and one SET per substate, and safe under the client's command retries), `is_hydrated` is flipped from the `OnLoadInternalState` leaf instead of the root (which made the redis manager fetch and persist every substate), and connecting no longer opens the whole state tree just to stamp the session id.

`State.hydrate` is unchanged and still used by the shared-state rehydrate and by the compatibility path for events arriving on an unknown token.

## Measurements

Production build of a 20-substate app with an `on_load` handler and a cookie var, redis state manager, behind a TCP proxy adding RTT and a 4 Mbps cap. Websocket compression disabled in the rig because granian (the production server) does not negotiate permessage-deflate. Medians of 7 to 9 fresh-session loads.

| Metric | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Time to hydrated, 40 ms RTT, 4 Mbps | 716 ms | 613 ms |
| Time to hydrated, zero latency | 236 ms | 195 ms |
| Hydrate payload on the wire | 36.5 KB | 2.1 KB |
| Websocket frames after connect | 3 out, 5 in | 0 out, 3 in |
| Redis commands per first load | 291 | 55 |
| Backend CPU per first load | 99 ms | about 70 ms |

Two further ideas were implemented, measured, and dropped: hydrating only the states a page renders (flat on both a light and a heavy app, and risky with `rx.memo` bodies), and enabling the opportunistic lock by default (55 to 34 redis commands, about 15 ms, but a locking-behavior change better left opt-in).

## Tests

- New unit tests: `hydrate_and_load` single-lock flow and cookie reset/apply, diffing against compiled defaults and the full-snapshot fallbacks, the one-command lock-checked tree save and its discard when the lock changed hands (run against both the mock and a real redis), the boot event carried in `on_connect` auth, a navigation queued behind a lock-waiting hydrate still receiving the snapshot, and a reconnect cancelling the previous page's unfinished `on_load` chain.
- Full unit suite green locally (`tests/units/reflex_cli` excluded: the hosting CLI rejects the dev version string, identical on the base commit).
- Browser integration tests run locally on the branch: client storage, connection banner (reconnect/rehydrate), dynamic routes, linked and shared state, navigation, state inheritance, event chains, login flow, router query, frontend path, mount target, stateless app, lifespan (240 passed).

description.body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> **This is a stopgap fix.** It is meant to unblock users until the real `ClientStateVar` refactor lands. The refactor will handle this case much more cleanly and **without creating extra React states** in components that only set the value. Treat this change as temporary: the refactor should replace it rather than build on it.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

### Description

Users reported frontend errors when sibling components share a global `rx._x.client_state` var (`global_ref=True`): one sibling renders `.value` and another sets it from a user interaction.

**Root cause:** `ClientStateVar.set` / `set_value()` returned a Var that referenced `refs['_client_state_set<name>']` but didn't carry the `useState`/`useId`/`refs` hooks that define it. Auto-memoization compiles the setter-only sibling into its own memo body, so the setter only worked if a component rendering `.value` had already mounted and defined the function. When no reader was mounted (for example, the reader sits behind an `rx.cond`), the setter threw:

```
TypeError: refs._client_state_set<name> is not a function
```

**Fix:**
- For global vars (`global_ref=True`), the setter Var now carries the `ClientStateVar`'s `VarData`. Every component that sets the value registers its own `useState` instance in the shared `refs` setter dict, and the global setter fans out to all of them.
- `create()` now keeps the default's full `VarData`, so a backend-derived default (`default=State.field`) brings its state `useContext` hook along.
- Local vars (`global_ref=False`) are unchanged. A setter-only sibling still fails loudly with `setX is not defined`, instead of silently updating a private copy of the state that no reader sees.

**Trade-offs of this stopgap (all addressed by the upcoming refactor):**
- Components that only set the value now hold an extra `useState` and re-render when the value changes.
- The setter's `useCallback` now lists the client-state hook values as dependencies, so it is recreated on every value change.
- With a backend-derived default (`default=State.field`), a setter-only component now also subscribes to that whole backend state through `useContext`. It re-renders, and recreates its `onClick`, on every delta to any field of that state, even though `useState` only reads the default on mount.
- Setter-only components also add an entry to `refs['_client_state_dict_set<name>']` that is never removed on unmount, as readers already did before this PR. Every set call still invokes the setters of unmounted components.

### Follow-ups for the `ClientStateVar` refactor

These are out of scope for this stopgap:
- Don't give setter-only components their own React state.
- Don't subscribe setter-only components to the default's backend state after mount.
- Remove per-instance entries from the setter and value dicts on unmount (e.g. `useEffect` cleanup).
- Allow backend `push()` / `retrieve()` to work when no component using the var is mounted. Today `run_script` can't carry hooks, so both require a mounted component. This is unchanged by this PR.
- Local (`global_ref=False`) vars still can't be shared between components that auto-memoize separately. This is inherent to local state and unchanged by this PR.

### Tests

- `tests/units/experimental/test_client_state.py` (new):
  - Global setters carry the client state hooks, for both `.set` and `.set_value(...)`.
  - Local setters don't carry them.
  - A backend-derived default's hooks reach `.value`, `.set` and `.set_value(...)`.
- `tests/units/compiler/test_memoize_plugin.py`: the memo for a setter-only sibling contains `useState` and defines the `refs` setter.
- `tests/integration/tests_playwright/test_client_state.py` (new): browser tests for three cases:
  - siblings that are both mounted
  - a setter clicked before its reader mounts behind an `rx.cond`
  - a backend-derived default with a sibling setter

The unit tests, the cond-reader browser test and the backend-default browser test fail without their fixes and pass with them. The both-mounted browser test also passed before the fix and is kept as a guard. The full unit suite passes, and ruff and pyright are clean.

description.body:
### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

### Changes To Core Features

- [x] Have you added an explanation of what your changes do and why you'd like us to include them?
- [x] Have you written new tests for your core changes, as applicable?
- [x] Have you successfully ran tests with your changes locally?

### Description

Two bugs in `EventProcessor.enqueue_stream_delta`, which buffered uploads (and custom routes) use to stream an event's deltas back over an HTTP response.

**1. The stream reused the root context's txid** (dccdc0574, 51e76b0e8)

The stream's context was `dataclasses.replace(self._root_context, ...)`, so its future and handler task were tracked under the root context's txid, which every top-level event names as its `parent_txid`. While a buffered upload was in flight (each of these reproduced before the fix):

- Every top-level event, from any client, was chained to the upload's future. Cancelling the upload (its client disconnecting) cancelled them too, and the upload's response stayed open until they finished.
- They inherited the upload's root generation, so a new navigation's `on_load` queued behind the previous page's unfinished one instead of superseding it.
- Concurrent uploads overwrote each other's `_futures`/`_tasks` entries: one stream ended early while its handler kept running untracked, and the other's future never resolved, hanging its response.

The stream's event now gets a context of its own: a fresh txid, no parent event, and the caller's OpenTelemetry context, so the handler span still nests under the upload request and records no `parent_txid`. The context is built in one step: CodSpeed flagged fork-then-`replace` at -4% on `test_yield_intermediate_update`, and a start/stream/stop round is back to `main`'s time locally.

**2. Deltas emitted after the stream ended were dropped** (587a4aefd)

Events chained from the streamed handler fork its context and inherit its delta emitter, so their deltas are streamed too, although the docstring said they were not. Streaming them is the behavior to keep: the frontend applies streamed chunks and socket messages through the same callbacks, and one channel keeps the chain's updates in order (browsers throttle XHR progress events, so a socket delta would overtake the handler's last streamed one). But anything emitted after the stream ended, such as by a recovery event the backend exception handler chains after the upload handler fails, went into a queue nobody read. The stream now takes deltas only until the chain finishes or the consumer leaves; later ones go out the usual way, and another token's delta is never yielded. The docstring now describes this.

**Also:** ports reflex-dev/reflex#7354's fix for the flaky `test_tree_phases_samples_a_real_tree` (627dfb11e), which failed `unit-tests (ubuntu-latest, 3.15)` here. The file matches that PR exactly, so whichever merges second applies it as a no-op.

**Not in this PR:** when the consumer leaves after the streamed handler itself finished, only the chained event being awaited gets cancelled; other running chained events continue.

### Test Plan

- Regression tests, each failing before its fix: `test_stream_delta_does_not_adopt_top_level_events`, `test_concurrent_stream_deltas_are_tracked_independently`, `test_stream_delta_emits_deltas_after_it_ends_normally`.
- Behavior pins: `test_stream_delta_yields_chained_event_deltas`, `test_stream_delta_sends_other_tokens_deltas_normally`, and `test_stream_delta_span_nests_under_caller` now asserts the span has no `parent_txid` attribute.
- `uv run pytest tests/units`: 11,027 passed, coverage 81.24% (the `reflex_bench` browser-driver tests were excluded locally, as they need a Playwright browser build that environment lacks). Event-processor and upload tests also pass on Python 3.10. `ruff` and `pyright` are clean.

description.body: Every backend event pays a fixed cost in the event processor and a per-value cost in the state machinery: reading fields and computed vars, wrapping values in mutable proxies, building the delta, encoding it to JSON and, with a redis or disk manager, pickling the touched states. Each of those paths did work per call that only has to happen once per class, per handler or per type, and a few did work that was never needed at all. Computed vars: a cache hit re-validated the whole cached value against the return type on every read (a 1000-element cached list cost ~1 ms per read; now ~0.2 us), the three cache attribute names were formatted per access, the last-updated timestamp was stored for every var although only interval vars read it, and marking a var dirty walked dependency dicts for names that have no dependents. The type mismatch is now logged once per computed value. Fields: scalar values skip the mutability check, and the dirty marking does not re-assign an already set touched flag through the dev-mode setattr hook. Mutable proxies: a proxy built for a list element no longer goes through the class lookup and the type-call dispatch, immutable values return before any tracking check in __getattr__, __getitem__ and __iter__, the dataclass frame check only runs for proxied dataclasses (via sys._getframe instead of a five-frame walk), and a method that is rebound to the proxy is no longer wrapped in a FunctionWrapper first. Event processor: the event context is built once per enqueue (fork takes the router_data), transaction ids come straight from os.urandom, the handler's coroutine-ness, background and supersedes flags and type hints are resolved once per handler, the per-event imports are hoisted, a handler that yields nothing skips the yield validation, the memory manager's modify_state and modify_state_with_links are plain async context managers instead of async generators, substate lookup resolves the class path once, and build_delta reads field values without constructing a proxy to unwrap. Serialization: json_dumps shares one encoder per set of separators instead of building a JSONEncoder per call, dataclasses serialize through a per-type serializer instead of dataclasses.fields() per instance, proxied values resolve their serializer once instead of dispatching twice, and StateUpdate serializes from a precomputed field tuple. State managers: redis persists every touched state of a tree in one pipeline instead of one write task (and one lock check) per state, deserializing a state updates the instance dict and drops the stale keys instead of filtering per key, the state-size check only runs on states over the limit, and the disk manager only derives a token for the states it writes. Measured on an idle 4-core VM (min of interleaved rounds): - in-process event pipeline, counter handler with 4 computed vars: 266 -> 205 us/event; 1000-row filtered/sorted table: 8.5 -> 4.4 ms/event - proxy iteration of 1000 dataclass rows: -55%; sorted(): -62%; attribute chains: -25%; write paths unchanged - cached computed var hit: 1.32 -> 0.19 us (scalar), 992 -> 0.19 us (list of 1000); scalar field read -35%, write -36% - JSON: 4-var delta 4.5 -> 2.7 us; 1000 proxied dataclass rows 2.5 -> 1.6 ms - redis manager, 35-state tree: 8.1 -> 2.1 ms/event; pickle 5.5 -> 3.3 us Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01DKCRZTdcqM4Smu9MKrjfhx

description.body: ### All Submissions: - [x] Have you followed the guidelines stated in [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/reflex-dev/reflex/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) file? - [x] Have you checked to ensure there aren't any other open [Pull Requests](https://github.com/reflex-dev/reflex/pulls) for the desired changed? ### Type of change - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) ### Changes To Core Features: - [x] Have you added an explanation of what your changes do and why you'd like us to include them? - [x] Have you written new tests for your core changes, as applicable? - [x] Have you successfully ran tests with your changes locally? ## What goes wrong `ArraySliceOperation._cached_var_name` renders a negative-step slice as the reversed forward slice `[end + 1 : start + 1]`. It has two bugs. 1. **Index `-1` wraps to `0`.** With `start == -1`, `start + 1` is `0`, so `State.items[-1::-1]` and `State.items[-1:-4:-1]` render `.slice(x, 0)` and evaluate to `[]`. Python gives the reversed list and `[5, 4, 3]`. With `end == -1`, `end + 1` is `0`, so `items[:-1:-1]` renders the whole list reversed where Python gives `[]`. String Vars go through the same code (`"hello"[-1::-1]` renders `""`). 2. **A Var step recurses forever.** The Var-step branch reads `self.step`, but the field is named `_step`. The attribute lookup falls through `Var.__getattr__` to `_cached_var_name` again, so `State.items[1:4:State.step]` raises `RecursionError` when it's rendered. ## Fix - Compute the reverse bounds once, mapping `-1` to the array length instead of `0`. An int bound is mapped statically. A Var bound gets `(bound === -1 ? arr.length : bound + 1)`. The reverse bounds are built only for a negative or Var step, so the positive-step path does no extra work. - Use the local `step` in the Var-step expression, and wrap the Var-step conditional in parentheses so that a following operation (e.g. `.length()`) applies to both branches. - For every other bound, the generated JS is unchanged. For example, the existing `[::-1]` assertion in `test_index_operation` still holds. ## Tests - `tests/units/test_var.py::test_slice_with_var_step` pins the Var-step expression. - `tests/units/test_var.py::test_var_step_slice_length_covers_both_branches` checks that `.length()` works for both step signs (Node). - `tests/units/test_var.py::test_negative_step_slices_match_python[step_var-bounds_var]` evaluates the generated JS in Node, which the test skips if Node isn't installed. It covers 9 negative-step slices (`[::-1]`, `[-1::-1]`, `[-1:-4:-1]`, `[:-1:-1]`, `[3::-1]`, `[4:0:-2]`, `[-2::-1]`, `[:-3:-1]`, `[-1::-2]`), each with every combination of int or Var step and int or Var bounds. It asserts every result equals Python's `items[s]`. - All of these fail on `main` (`fe2a78f4`): the int case gets `[]` instead of `[5, 4, 3, 2, 1]`, and the Var cases raise `RecursionError`. They pass with the fix. Checks, all run locally: - `uv run pytest tests/units`: 9849 passed. - `pre-commit run --from-ref HEAD~1 --to-ref HEAD`: ruff-format, ruff-check, codespell, update-pyi-files, pyright and ty all pass. - A news fragment is added under `packages/reflex-base/news/`. AI disclosure: an AI agent (Claude) found this bug and wrote the patch and tests, operating the `breken-ai` account. I reviewed the diff adversarially before opening this PR. I'll respond to review feedback, including Greptile/Copilot.
description.title: fix: negative-step Var slices at -1 and slices with a Var step

description.body:
### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

### What / why

`reflex db makemigrations` and `reflex db migrate --autogenerate` crash with a
`sqlalchemy.exc.CompileError` when the autogenerated migration adds a column that
has a **callable default** to an existing table. This is the single most common
real-world schema change: adding a `created` timestamp or a UUID column, e.g.

```python
created: datetime.datetime = rx.Field(default_factory=datetime.datetime.now)
# or
id: uuid.UUID = rx.Field(default=uuid.uuid4)
```

Root cause is in the `AddColumnOp` rewriter registered during autogeneration in
`reflex/model.py`. To carry a sqlmodel default onto existing rows, it copies the
column default into a `server_default` by wrapping `op.column.default.arg` in
`sqlalchemy.literal(...)`:

```python
if op.column.default is not None and op.column.server_default is None:
    op.column.server_default = sqlalchemy.DefaultClause(
        sqlalchemy.sql.expression.literal(op.column.default.arg),
    )
```

For a **scalar** default (`Field(default=7)`) `op.column.default.arg` is the value
(`7`), which renders fine. For a **callable** default, SQLAlchemy stores a
`CallableColumnDefault` whose `.arg` is the Python function object itself, not a
value. `literal(<function>)` becomes a bind parameter with `NullType`, and when
the migration script is rendered with `literal_binds=True` SQLAlchemy raises:

```
sqlalchemy.exc.CompileError: No literal value renderer is available for literal
value "<function datetime.now at 0x...>" with datatype NULL
```

so migration-script generation aborts.

### Fix

Gate the `server_default` rewrite on `op.column.default.is_scalar`, so only scalar
defaults are carried as a SQL literal:

```python
if (
    op.column.default is not None
    and op.column.default.is_scalar
    and op.column.server_default is None
):
    ...
```

Callable defaults then keep alembic's default behavior (no `server_default`), which
is correct: a per-row Python callable cannot be represented as a single SQL literal.
Scalar `server_default` behavior is unchanged. `is_scalar` is defined on the base
`DefaultGenerator` (class-level `False`), so this is safe for every default type
alembic can attach.

### Tests

Added `tests/units/test_model.py::test_automigration_add_column_with_callable_default`,
which creates a table, migrates to head, then adds callable-default columns
(`default_factory=datetime.now`, a nullable `default_factory`) and runs the
autogenerate/migrate path. It fails with the `CompileError` above on `main` and
passes with the fix. It also asserts that a scalar default alongside the callable
one still works and that rows read back correctly.

Local checks (all green):

```
uv run pytest tests/units/test_model.py     # 6 passed
uv run ruff check reflex/model.py tests/units/test_model.py
uv run ruff format --check reflex/model.py tests/units/test_model.py
uv run pyright reflex/model.py tests/units/test_model.py    # 0 errors
```
description.title: fix(model): only carry scalar column defaults as server_default in migrations
